questions.q: Why does the Meridian Wealth Partners design set Household__c's OWD to Private rather than Public Read Only?
options: Private is always required for any object with over a million records
Public Read Only is not a valid OWD setting for custom objects
The regulatory-review carve-out is a stronger compliance posture when it narrows from a Private baseline than when it has to fight against a firm-wide-visible default
Private is required because Compliance needs edit access
questions.explain: Starting from Private and granting explicitly (role hierarchy, the Compliance rule) gives a cleaner, stronger compliance story than starting broad and trying to carve out an exception from it.

questions.q: Why are Private Banking and Retail Advisory modeled as two separate role-hierarchy branches instead of one shared tree?
options: Salesforce technically forbids more than one branch under the root
Separate branches are required whenever an org has more than 1,000 users
It reduces the object's record count
It satisfies 'Retail Advisors must never see Private Banking households' structurally, rather than relying on a sharing rule that could be misconfigured
questions.explain: Keeping the two business lines on non-overlapping branches makes the required separation a property of the hierarchy's shape, not something a fallible rule has to enforce correctly every time.

questions.q: Why does the design use a Restriction Rule, rather than a second sharing rule, to limit visibility of regulatory-review households?
options: Sharing rules are strictly additive and cannot subtract access that the role hierarchy or another rule already granted
Restriction Rules are cheaper to run at scale than sharing rules
Sharing rules cannot reference checkbox fields in their criteria
Restriction Rules automatically notify Compliance when triggered
questions.explain: A Restriction Rule is the one declarative mechanism that removes visibility from what the role hierarchy and other grants would otherwise show, which is exactly what the regulatory-review requirement needs.

questions.q: Why does the design use manual sharing, rather than a new permanent sharing rule or team structure, for the Private Banking / Retail Advisory cross-sell transitions?
options: Manual sharing is required by regulation for any cross-business-line access
The situation is rare and temporary (under 50 households at a time), so a permanent mechanism would add ongoing complexity to solve a small, short-lived need
Teams cannot be created on Household__c
Manual sharing is the only mechanism compatible with Restriction Rules
questions.explain: Building a dedicated permanent mechanism for a consistently low-volume, temporary scenario would add maintenance burden disproportionate to the actual need; manual sharing, applied and removed per case, fits better.

questions.q: What access does the Compliance sharing rule grant, and why not more?
options: Read/Write on all Households, because Compliance may need to correct records during an audit
Read Only limited to only the Retail Advisory branch
Read Only on all Households firm-wide, since Compliance needs visibility for audit purposes but should never edit client data
Full object-level Modify All permission
questions.explain: The stated requirement is audit visibility without edit rights, so the rule grants Read Only across both business lines rather than a broader or narrower level of access.
